question: Ravi can complete one-fourth of the total work in 15 days, Chavi can complete one-third of the total work in 18 days, Dhani can complete half of the total work in 24 days. In how much time can Ravi, Chavi and Dhani complete three-fourth of the work together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Days to complete the whole work: Ravi = 15 × 4 = 60, Chavi = 18 × 3 = 54, Dhani = 24 × 2 = 48.

Total Work = LCM(60, 54, 48) = 2160 units.

Combined Efficiency = 2160/60 + 2160/54 + 2160/48 = 36 + 40 + 45 = 121 units/day.

Time required for 3/4 work = (3/4 × 2160) ÷ 121 = 1620/121 = 13 ⁴⁷/₁₂₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ⁴⁷/₁₂₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ravi completes 1/4 of the work in 15 days.

Chavi completes 1/3 of the work in 18 days.

Dhani completes 1/2 of the work in 24 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total days taken by Ravi to complete the whole work = 15 × 4 = 60 days

⇒ Total days taken by Chavi to complete the whole work = 18 × 3 = 54 days

⇒ Total days taken by Dhani to complete the whole work = 24 × 2 = 48 days

⇒ Let the total work be the LCM of 60, 54, and 48.

⇒ Total efficiency of Ravi, Chavi, and Dhani = 36 + 40 + 45 = 121 units/day

⇒ Target work to be completed = 3/4 of Total Work = 3/4 × 2160 = 1620 units

⇒ Time required by all three together = 1620 ÷ 121 days

⇒ Time taken = 13 ⁴⁷/₁₂₁ days

**∴ The correct answer is 13 ⁴⁷/₁₂₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the work done. If people work together for the same number of days, their wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept works identically to Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (fill the tank), while outlet pipes have negative efficiency (empty the tank).

Alternate Days Work

When workers take turns on alternate days, calculate the total work done in a complete block (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers), multiply to get near the total work, and finally add the remaining portion for the last working person.
